name: Seagonia Crab Co.
notes: Own Instagram bio lists Kakaʻako Sat 8-12 and Ono Grindz & Makeke Thu 4-8. Bio does not list Kailua, so that stop is unconfirmed. Star-Advertiser (2024) says orders are in person or by Instagram DM. No Facebook page or website found. Bio snapshot is undated, so still_active is null. Side is town (Kakaʻako).

name: I Heart Kimchi
notes: Only a third-party mention: a 2026 HAWAIʻI Magazine Kailua guide names kimchi from I Heart Kimchi at the KailuaTown Farmers Market. No own website, Instagram or Facebook found, and I did not guess handles. still_active is true on that single mention only. Side is windward.

name: Nosh Hawaiʻi
notes: Website and contact are on the Hawaiʻi Farm Bureau (organizer) KCC vendor page. The Farm Bureau Nosh LLC page lists Thursday Kailua and Saturday KCC. Instagram and Facebook handles come from a Honolulu Magazine article (about 2020) that gave @nosh_hawaii and facebook.com/noshhawaii. I did not confirm those accounts are live. A 2026 HAWAIʻI Magazine piece recommends Nosh Hawaiʻi at the Kailua Farmers Market. Third-party listings give a Honolulu address and no Kailua base, so side is null.

name: Chef Arnaud Jager
notes: Event listing: French omelet station at KailuaTown Farmers Market, Sunday Sep 27, 8AM-12PM, 640 Ulukahiki St. The date has passed, and I found no later confirmation. The business is registered as Chef Arnaud LLC, Kaneohe (BBB), which is why side is windward. No own website or social accounts found, and I did not guess handles.

name: JOJA Hawaii
notes: The Makeke Maps vendor page gives Instagram @joja.hawaii, and TikTok posts tag the same handle. I did not open the Instagram page itself. That page says JOJA has its own site, but no URL was shown, so website is null. Third-party pages (NateEatsHawaii) list Kakaʻako Saturdays 7:30-12. Other sources conflict on the second weekly stop (Waikiki Beachwalk, Monday vs Saturday), so I did not set a schedule URL. A TikTok roundup updated about 12 days ago still shows the Kakaʻako stand. Side is town.

name: MAʻO Organic Farms
notes: Own CSA page lists Saturday pickups and market stops, including Kakaʻako Farmers Market 8am-12pm. The page snapshot may be dated. A 2026 third-party article (wanderlustyle) confirms produce at the Kakaʻako Farmers Market. No Instagram or Facebook URL found in results. The farm is in Waiʻanae, so side is leeward_ewa; the Kakaʻako stand is a market stop.

name: Islander Sake Brewery
notes: Own site says the brewery took a temporary break from the Kakaʻako Farmers Market from end of Dec 2024 and will return with renewed products. It also announces a new brewery at Hapuna on Hawaiʻi Island. The shop location page (undated) still lists a Saturday Kakaʻako market stand and a Honolulu location at 25 N. King St. I could not tell whether the market stand has resumed or whether the Oʻahu operation continues. Social accounts not found. Side is town.

name: Roscoe's Sourdough Breads
notes: Only third-party sources found (Onolicious, Paper Plane, Forbes 2019). They place the stand at the Kakaʻako Farmers Market on Saturdays. No own website, Instagram or Facebook found, and I did not guess handles. No dated 2026 source, so still_active is null. Side is town.

name: Wallflour Bake Shop
notes: Own site says to follow @wallflourbakeshop for new items and schedule updates, which is why the schedule URL is the Instagram. A third-party listing says Kakaʻako every Saturday and KailuaTown 2nd and 4th Sundays; this is undated. Past Monday pop-ups at ʻIliʻili Cash & Carry and pre-orders are described as suspended. No dated 2026 source, so still_active is null. No Facebook found. Side is town.

name: Izu's Mochi
notes: Third-party sources (Onolicious, Paper Plane) say it has a Saturday stand at Kakaʻako and takes pre-orders by Instagram DM. Paper Plane says the account is private, and neither source gives the handle, so I left it null. No website or Facebook found. No dated 2026 source, so still_active is null. Side is town.

name: Youpo Noodles
notes: The Farm Bureau (organizer) vendor page, about 71 days old, gives the website and email and lists the Thursday Kailua Farmers' Market. It lists the restaurant at 1109 Maunakea St, Honolulu. Honolulu Magazine says Youpo opened a Chinatown restaurant after its farmers market run. Neither source confirms the Kakaʻako stand is current. No Instagram or Facebook found. Side is town.

name: Daguzan Charcuterie
notes: Own Find us page lists Saturday at Kakaʻako Farmers Market and Sunday at the Kailua market, plus retail and online sales. The Instagram handle @daguzan_charcuterie comes from a House of Mana Up article that names it for this brand. I did not open the Instagram page. Based in Kaneohe, so side is windward. The site pages are undated. No Facebook found.

name: The Rice Factory
notes: Onolicious says the market stand sells rice, soy sauce, musubi and vinegar drinks, and that the business also has a nearby brick-and-mortar store. No own website or social accounts found, and I did not guess handles. The Onolicious post is about 509 days old, so still_active is null. Side is town.

name: Dean & Deluca
notes: Own site says Dean & DeLuca Hawaii products are sold only at the Waikiki stores and at the Kakaʻako farmers market every Saturday, with no online sales. That notice and the site's FarmLovers market post are old (about 466+ days). The Instagram handle comes from a Honolulu Magazine market feature that names it for this vendor. It looks like the Ritz-Carlton store account, so I treated it as medium. A late-2025 third-party article still lists the Kakaʻako stand. Independently operated in Waikiki and Kakaʻako. No Facebook found. Side is town.

name: Wicked HI
notes: An Aloha State Daily article (Jan 2026) says the business is now Nomadic, formerly Wicked HI, and gives Instagram @nomadic.hi. It has a Haleʻiwa food truck and a new Kailua shop at 270 Kuulei Rd. The Facebook page 'Wicked Hi Slush' (Haleiwa) is the older brand page. The website wickedhicafe.com is the café site found in results; the Facebook page lists wickedhislushie.com. I did not verify which site is current after the rebrand. Onolicious (old) says the Kakaʻako stand sells only honey slush on Saturdays. No source confirms the Kakaʻako stand is current under either name. Business is based in Waialua/Haleʻiwa, so side is north_shore.
